papers.title: Recognition and mechanism of M. tuberculosis cell wall galactan transport.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of M. tuberculosis WzmWzt, a polysaccharide ABC transporter, reveal how lipid-linked galactan is recognized and translocated: substrate binding through two Wzm and two Wzt subunits, gate-helix extension priming Wzt dimerization, and ATP-driven conformational change. Mutagenesis identifies residues essential for transport, informing cell-wall-targeted anti-tubercular drug development.

papers.title: TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 links bacteria recognition to autophagosome formation in xenophagy.
papers.summary: During Salmonella infection, TBK1 phosphorylates WIPI2 at Ser96, strengthening its interaction with ATG16L1 on Salmonella-containing vacuoles and with PI3P. This recruits WIPI2 to bacteria, promoting localized phagophore expansion and efficient bacterial clearance, revealing how bacterial recognition is coupled to autophagosome formation in xenophagy.

papers.title: Live visualization of dynamic autophagy processes in LC3 reporter mice using enhanced two-photon microscopy.
papers.summary: An enhanced intravital two-photon imaging framework, combining tissue stabilization, deep-learning denoising, and eSRRF super-resolution, enables real-time visualization of LC3-positive autophagic structures in mouse liver and skeletal muscle during starvation, ischemia, and ethanol exposure. Chloroquine-based flux assays distinguish increased autophagosome formation from impaired degradation, enabling functional in vivo autophagy analysis.

papers.title: Alphavirus Nsp3 protein hijacks receptor-mediated mitophagy via BNIP3L/NIX to dampen IFN response and promote viral replication.
papers.summary: Alphavirus Nsp3 proteins from Getah, chikungunya, and Sindbis viruses directly trigger receptor-mediated mitophagy by binding BNIP3L/NIX. This mitophagy degrades MAVS, dampening type I interferon responses and promoting viral replication. BNIP3L knockdown alleviates mitophagy, identifying Nsp3 as a virulence factor that co-opts mitochondrial quality control for immune evasion.

papers.title: A neuronal GPCR modifies neuropeptide signaling to suppress proteostasis in distal tissues.
papers.summary: In C. elegans, knockdown of the neuronal GPCR GTR-1 differentially reshapes neuropeptide gene expression and suppresses protein aggregation in tissues expressing distinct proteotoxic proteins, while enhancing protein degradation. The findings position neuronal neuropeptide signaling as an organism-level coordinator of proteostasis relevant to neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Cell heterogeneity contributes to the variable response of HIV-1 to latency-reversing agents.
papers.summary: Using dual-copy MS2 tagging and mathematical modeling of live-cell HIV-1 transcription, basal proviral activity was uncorrelated within cells, reflecting promoter-intrinsic noise. Latency-reversing agents shifted variability toward cell-state-driven correlation, with variable drug-target effects across cells, showing how cellular heterogeneity shapes HIV-1 reactivation and latency-reversing strategies.

papers.title: A helix-loop-helix gene orchestrates male fate in common carp.
papers.summary: A male-specific helix-loop-helix gene in common carp encodes Pangu, a Sertoli-cell peptide shown by loss- and gain-of-function analyses to be necessary and sufficient for male sex determination. Pangu represses cyp19a1a, the key ovarian-differentiation regulator, establishing the first master sex-determining gene in Cyprinidae.

papers.title: Canonical Wnt induction by OTULIN prevents keratinocyte death and skin inflammation.
papers.summary: OTULIN, a linear-ubiquitin-specific deubiquitinase, promotes canonical Wnt signaling in keratinocytes by regulating linear ubiquitination of beta-catenin. Stabilizing beta-catenin in OTULIN-deficient keratinocytes prevents TNF-induced cell death and skin inflammation by preserving TCF3/4, identifying linear deubiquitination as a key regulator of epithelial viability and Wnt signaling.

papers.title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth.
papers.summary: The mitotic kinase CIT phosphorylates the splicing regulator THRAP3, directing its RNA binding to CIT-dependent pre-mRNA targets involved in proliferation. Antisense oligos blocking THRAP3 recruitment to CIT-dependent sites inhibit prostate cancer growth across cell lines and patient-derived organoids without affecting benign cells, defining a therapeutic splicing vulnerability.

papers.title: HPSC-derived mesenchymal stromal cells ameliorate murine autistic-like phenotypes through activating oxytocinergic neurons.
papers.summary: iPSC-derived mesenchymal stromal cells alleviate anxiety, grooming, and social deficits in Shank3B knockout and BTBR autism model mice. Infused MSCs localize to the neurohypophysis and activate oxytocin neurons via secreted prostaglandin E2; disrupting PGE2 synthesis abolishes efficacy, revealing an MSC-oxytocinergic neuroendocrine mechanism for improving autism-related behaviors.

papers.title: Senescent tumor cell membrane-based "time engine" nanosystem amplifies endoplasmic reticulum targeting for metastasis blockade.
papers.summary: A sequential 'time engine' nanosystem uses senescent tumor cell membrane-coated nanoparticles: ribociclib-loaded particles first induce tumor cell senescence and disrupt the cytoskeleton, then brefeldin A-loaded particles exploit heightened senescent-cell endoplasmic reticulum targeting to trigger intense ER stress. This achieves strong ER accumulation and antimetastatic efficacy in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice.

papers.title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21.
papers.summary: Exon 2 inclusion drives SUV39H2 overexpression in CDK4/6-inhibitor-resistant breast cancer, correlating with poor prognosis. GAPmer antisense oligonucleotides or methyltransferase inhibition against SUV39H2 restores p21 transcription via H3K9me3 removal at enhancers, reinstating therapy-induced senescence and offering a rational combination strategy to overcome CDK4/6i resistance.

papers.title: Enhancer binding kinetics explain transcription factor hub formation.
papers.summary: Live imaging of Dorsal TF hubs in Drosophila embryos shows hub enrichment and persistence scale with enhancer binding-motif number, yet do not predict transcriptional bursting. Computational modeling demonstrates TF-DNA binding kinetics alone explains hub formation, supporting a model where hubs arise from enhancer-encoded interactions rather than higher-order regulatory assemblies.

papers.title: Phage-ICE tandems facilitate bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance spread.
papers.summary: Phage-ICE tandems, formed by site-specific accretion of prophages and integrative conjugative elements, are widespread across bacterial phyla. Phage integrases drive excision while ICE machinery mediates transfer; recombination-based fail-safe routes enable cotransfer of chromosomal DNA, remodeling transcription and accelerating antimicrobial resistance dissemination in multidrug-resistant pathogens.

papers.title: Extracellular matrix-targeted TNC-scFv armoring enhances CAR T cell persistence and antitumor activity in solid tumors.
papers.summary: An armored CAR T platform secretes a tenascin-C-specific scFv targeting the extracellular matrix of solid tumors. TNC armoring enhances cytotoxicity, persistence, and reduces exhaustion, reprogramming the tumor microenvironment toward CD8-positive functional T cells. In humanized models, armored cells mediate robust antitumor responses with minimal toxicity and support combinatorial IL-2 armoring.

papers.title: SUMO2 deletion changes chromatin accessibility and enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and tumor infiltration.
papers.summary: T cell-specific SUMO2 deletion enhances CD8+ T cell activation by opening chromatin at AP-1 family enhancer regions including BATF and JUNB, without increasing interferon-I responsive genes. SUMO2 knockout CAR T and OT1 cells show greater tumor infiltration and growth inhibition, suggesting SUMOylation blockade as a strategy to enhance adoptive T cell therapy.

papers.title: Carbonic anhydrase VIII regulates IP3R1-dependent Ca(2+) signaling to coordinate insulin secretion and hepatic glucose production.
papers.summary: Carbonic anhydrase VIII, an endogenous IP3R1 inhibitor, coordinately regulates glucose-induced insulin secretion in pancreas and hepatic glucose production. CAR8 deficiency amplifies calcium oscillations via heightened IP3R1 sensitivity, and hepatic CAR8 restoration in obese diabetic mice reduces excessive glucose production, identifying cross-organ calcium signaling as a diabetes-relevant axis.

papers.title: ALIX-dependent small extracellular vesicles from tissue-resident mesenchymal cells regulate pancreatic β cell proliferation in obesity.
papers.summary: Mice lacking ALIX in PDGFRalpha-positive mesenchymal progenitors produce fewer small extracellular vesicles and, under high-fat diet, show impaired glucose tolerance with reduced pancreatic beta cell area despite preserved insulin sensitivity. Mesenchymal EVs promote beta cell proliferation, identifying ALIX-dependent vesicle biogenesis as a regulator of metabolic adaptation in obesity.

papers.title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip.
papers.summary: A microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip recreates gut oxygen gradients and perfuses probiotic metabolites to human cartilage organoids without cross-contamination. Multiomics and patient-derived organoid assays suggest probiotic metabolites promote cartilage anabolism via PI3K and MAPK pathways, upregulating collagen II and aggrecan while suppressing metalloproteinases, providing a preclinical platform for probiotic osteoarthritis therapeutics.

papers.title: SMCHD1 is a target for gene activation therapy to treat Prader-Willi syndrome.
papers.summary: SMCHD1 represses the imprinted Prader-Willi syndrome locus in mice and humans, silencing the entire cluster in neural lineages. Post-developmental SMCHD1 deletion activates paternal genes in hypothalamus and improves phenotypes in a PWS mouse model with apparent safety, supporting SMCHD1 targeting as gene-activation therapy for Prader-Willi syndrome.

papers.title: A bifunctional actuator to correct loss-of-function deficits in cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels.
papers.summary: A genetically encoded bifunctional nanobody actuator for cardiac Nav1.5 combines a peptide restoring proper inactivation with a linkage-specific deubiquitinase promoting channel surface localization. Validated in heterologous systems and human and mouse cardiomyocytes, it corrects both gating and trafficking defects, providing a framework for multifunctional correction of ion channelopathies.

papers.title: Long-term immunoprophylaxis by TLR9 ligand mediates macrophage-ILC cross-talk against respiratory viral infection.
papers.summary: A single intranasal dose of CpG oligodeoxynucleotide-schizophyllan complex (K3-SPG) confers antigen-independent protection against lethal respiratory virus infection for up to 100 days. Protection involves biphasic innate activation: early macrophage-mediated defense followed by epigenetically reprogrammed innate lymphoid cells, dependent on TLR9 and TNF-alpha, supporting adjuvant-based immunoprophylaxis against respiratory viruses.

papers.title: Dishevelled-mediated clustering stabilizes Frizzled6 and Vangl2 to establish planar cell polarity in the mammalian skin.
papers.summary: Using endogenously tagged fluorescent reporters in embryonic mouse epidermis, Dishevelled proteins coaccumulate with Frizzled6 in polarized puncta and stabilize planar cell polarity complexes. The oligomerizing Dix domain of Dvl3, previously associated with Wnt signaling, is required for Dvl3 asymmetric localization, revealing a role for Dvl oligomerization in PCP assembly.

papers.title: Influenza A virus infection induces immune dysregulation in the placenta and fetus without vertical transmission in nonhuman primates.
papers.summary: In pregnant pigtail macaques infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, maternal infection caused stillbirth in 18% of pregnancies without vertical transmission. Maternal infection induced placental type I interferon responses and altered fetal immune cell populations including CD4/CD8 T cells and monocytes, with fetal immunity more strongly linked to maternal disease severity than placental perturbation.

papers.title: Standardizing Cell Ontology terms for cross-study integration in the female reproductive tract.
papers.summary: An international collaboration harmonized Cell Ontology terminology for the female reproductive tract, standardizing annotations of ovarian, fallopian tube, and uterine cell populations from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. Supported by marker gene sets and anatomical linkages, this shared reference framework enables cross-study integration and consistent classification of reproductive cell types.

papers.title: Chromatin interaction landscape of epimorphic regeneration in teleost fish.
papers.summary: Micro-C mapping of zebrafish fin regeneration shows chromatin loop reorganization dominates over TAD and compartment changes during blastema formation. Injury-altered loops affect morphogenesis and cell division genes; perturbing altered loops at the il11a locus suppresses expression and impairs regeneration, with CTCF/CTCFL and ATF7 motifs enriched at loop anchors across teleost species.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of E. coli MscL in lipid nanodiscs combined with solid-state NMR in liposomes capture closed-state structure and the conformational dynamics of the low-threshold G22S mutant. Lipid-protein interactions emerge as key determinants of mechanosensitive gating, establishing a synergistic structural framework for studying and engineering mechanogating.

papers.title: Rapid protamine evolution suppresses meiotic drive in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Gene replacement experiments in Drosophila show that rapid protamine evolution is driven by meiotic drive suppression. Divergent MST77F orthologs cause X-sperm DNA compaction defects and male-biased progeny; dosage-dependent rescue reveals MST77F protects the X chromosome from a killer-target drive system, explaining relentless protamine sequence diversification across species.

papers.title: Translocation-induced enhancer rewiring reveals cryptic oncogenic circuits in multiple myeloma.
papers.summary: Transfinder, a multiomic pipeline combining long-read sequencing, Hi-C, epigenomic profiling, and RNA-seq, decodes enhancer-promoter neo-loops at translocation breakpoints in multiple myeloma. It reveals t(16;22) co-activates RAB36 alongside MAF and identifies new translocations activating MYC and CBX7, uncovering cryptic oncogenic circuits and clinically actionable noncoding dependencies.

papers.title: A biohybrid mesh harvester for distributed energy harvesting in living tissues.
papers.summary: A biohybrid mesh harvester embeds individual energy-harvesting units within a tissue-like network, achieving cell-scale integration with cardiac tissue and distributed biomechanical energy conversion. Effective energy density exceeds centralized substrate-attached approaches by over an order of magnitude, providing a generalizable framework for powering bio-integrated electronics in living tissues.

papers.title: Real-time single-molecule imaging in zebrafish embryos uncovers noncanonical translation.
papers.summary: Real-time single-molecule imaging of bmp2b translation in zebrafish embryos using ALFA nascent-chain labeling and lattice light-sheet microscopy reveals that only a subset of mRNAs are actively translated. Translation operates below maximal initiation, with the bmp2b 5'UTR supporting cap-independent translation, providing a quantitative framework for in vivo translational kinetics.

papers.title: Clonal lineage tracing and parallel multiomics profiling reveal transcriptional heterogeneity induced by ARID1A deficiency.
papers.summary: Combining clonal lineage tracing with single-cell multiomics shows ARID1A deficiency broadens chromatin accessibility and increases transcriptional variability within and across clones without conferring a fixed phenotype. Variable clones show no growth advantage in standard conditions but are preferentially recovered under stress and during lung colonization, consistent with bet-hedging tumor evolution.

papers.title: Self-buoyant cell-spheroid culture programming multi-spheroid assembly.
papers.summary: A self-buoyant spheroid culture platform uses microbubbles to lift one-drop-one-spheroid levitation growth without external fields, then enables rapid spheroid transfer, media exchange, and drug administration via droplet 'kiss' contacts. Programmable multi-spheroid assembly and fusion generate 'buoyantoids,' supporting mass production of assembloids for tissue engineering and high-throughput drug screening.

papers.title: Human trilayer engineered blood vessel reveals influence of fibroblasts on disease progression in model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria.
papers.summary: A human trilayer tissue-engineered blood vessel with endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and fibroblasts models Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. HGPS fibroblasts substantially elevate vascular pathology, base editing corrects disease features, and cell-combination analysis assigns ECM dysregulation and fibrosis to fibroblasts, collagen accumulation to SMCs, and inflammation to ECs.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco.
papers.summary: Structure-informed machine learning (ESM-IF1) guided directed evolution of Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco, identifying variants improving catalytic efficiency beyond natural plant sequence diversity. The T391I substitution increases carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%, demonstrating ML-assisted protein engineering potential for enhancing crop photosynthesis and productivity.

papers.title: Targeted integration of extrachromosomal arrays in C. elegans using PhiC31 integrase.
papers.summary: PhiC31 integrase enables efficient targeted integration of C. elegans extrachromosomal arrays at attB landing sites across three chromosomes, with Cas9-directed repair templates enabling arbitrary genomic sites. Single injections integrate arrays up to 18 megabases, including a strain incorporating 65% of the yeast genome, replacing unstable arrays with stable integrated transgenes.

papers.title: Cis-regulatory inactivation of vitamin D signaling confers extreme calcium tolerance in Jialing fish.
papers.summary: Jialing fish thriving in China's hypercalcemic karst lakes evolved extreme calcium tolerance through cis-regulatory loss of vitamin D signaling. Lake fish show over 90% suppression of gill vdrb and near-loss of downstream calb2a, driven by enhancer mutations; zebrafish knockouts of either gene enhance survival under hypercalcemia, illustrating regulatory dismantling as adaptation.

papers.title: Endogenous retrovirus control of calbindin is essential for human early embryogenesis.
papers.summary: A HERVH endogenous retrovirus integration on chromosome 8q21.3, acquired during homininae evolution, drives calbindin (CALB1) expression in human preimplantation embryos and embryonic stem cells. CALB1 expression is essential for ESC growth, senescence prevention, and blastoid and amnioid formation, showing co-opted retroviral regulation echoes essential developmental requirements.

papers.title: Epigenetic insights into extreme longevity in the world's oldest terrestrial animal, Jonathan.
papers.summary: Genome and methylome sequencing of Jonathan, a 194-year-old Aldabra giant tortoise, reveals unique variants in aging pathways and substantial methylation changes versus younger tortoises. Low-entropy methylome regions enrich for mitochondrial electron transport and RNA metabolism gene promoters, linking transcriptional fidelity in energy production and RNA processing to extreme longevity.

papers.title: Herpes simplex virus pUL56 abolishes neuronal activity by removing voltage-gated ion channels from the plasma membrane.
papers.summary: HSV-1 infection of human iPSC-derived cortical neurons extensively remodels the plasma membrane proteome, removing voltage-gated sodium, potassium, and calcium channels and abolishing synchronized calcium signaling. The viral ubiquitin-ligase adaptor pUL56 is the principal effector; pUL56 expression alone suffices to silence neuronal activity, identifying a potent viral suppressor of excitability.

papers.title: Integrative genotype-environment association and single-cell transcriptomic analyses identify candidate mechanisms of environmental adaptation in pigs.
papers.summary: Integrating genotype-environment association analysis across 1,151 pig genomes from 146 populations with lung single-cell transcriptomics identifies candidate adaptation genes, including ASXL1 for high-altitude adaptation and NOTCH signaling pathways overlooked by traditional methods. The study reveals regulatory complexity underlying pig environmental adaptation following human-mediated global dispersal.

papers.title: Coordinated mitochondrial quality control underlies oxidative stress resilience in MUSE stem cells.
papers.journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
papers.summary: MUSE stem cells resist oxidative stress better than conventional MSCs, showing lower ROS accumulation, preserved mitochondrial DNA integrity, rapid antioxidant and DNA repair gene induction, and enhanced mitophagy via PINK1/phospho-ubiquitin-S65 signaling. Coordinated mitochondrial biogenesis through PGC-1alpha/NRF2 activation underlies a remove-and-replace quality control program preserving mitochondrial function.

papers.title: MyoD and Myogenin regulatory cascade is targeted by tumor signals to repress myogenesis in cancer cachexia.
papers.summary: In cancer cachexia, tumor signals repress the MyoD-Myogenin regulatory cascade in muscle stem cells: MyoD transactivation and its transcriptional activation via the distal enhancer core element are suppressed, blocking myogenic regeneration. MyoD or Myogenin overexpression rescues myogenesis, identifying MyoD dysfunction as central to cachectic muscle wasting.

papers.title: New insights into Müllerian duct differentiation provided by single cell transcriptomics in the chicken embryo.
papers.summary: Single-cell transcriptomics of chicken Mullerian ducts defines epithelial and mesenchymal signatures, identifying DKK4 as an AMH-responsive Wnt antagonist sufficient to induce duct regression. Female embryos show asymmetric duct fate with right-duct regression transcriptionally distinct from male regression, revealing sexual divergence in Mullerian duct differentiation mechanisms.

papers.title: Combined lactate- and phosphate-dependent cytoplasmic acidification is associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth arrest at acidic pH.
papers.summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth arrest at acidic pH on lactate depends on phosphate uptake: lactate plus phosphate acidifies the cytoplasm below pH 6.7 and stresses proton motive force, while phot or pstc2 mutants maintain neutral cytoplasmic pH. Low phosphate induces SenX3-RegX3 signaling, linking pH homeostasis to mycobacterial acid stress physiology.

papers.title: The generation and characterization of CTRP9-Cre(ERT2) knock-in mice for targeting endothelial cell muscle and adipose tissues.
papers.summary: CTRP9 was identified as a selective marker of muscle and adipose microvascular endothelial cells from scRNA-seq data. A CRISPR-generated CTRP9-CreERT2-tdTomato knock-in mouse line enables inducible, specific targeting of this endothelial population across heart, skeletal muscle, tongue, and adipose tissue, providing a tool to study muscle endothelial biology.

papers.title: Geographic barrier contributed to the diversity of maternal and paternal lineages in New Guinea Island.
papers.summary: Mitochondrial and Y chromosome sequencing of 163 individuals across New Guinea reveals strong geographic structuring, a west-east split around 20-30 thousand years ago, and higher mtDNA diversity than NRY diversity consistent with patrilocal social structure. The central range acted as a significant geographic barrier, supporting a northern migration route into Sahul.

papers.title: Milestones in O-GlcNAc Research: Technological Advances that Shaped the Field.
papers.summary: A historical review of O-GlcNAcylation research traces how technological advances shaped the field: enzymatic labeling probes, O-GlcNAc-specific antibodies, enzyme cloning enabling inhibitors and genetics, electron transfer dissociation mass spectrometry for glycoproteomics, and bioorthogonal chemistry for live-cell studies, collectively establishing O-GlcNAc as a central regulator of cellular metabolism.

papers.title: A phosphoinositide and RAB switch controls early macropinocytosis.
papers.summary: VPS34-derived PI3P determines macropinosome fate: VPS34 inhibition prevents Rab5a recruitment and early endosomal identity, instead accumulating recycling regulators Rab8a, Rab10, Rab11a, and PI4P that drive fusion with the plasma membrane. Rab5a establishes endosomal identity while Rab8a mediates membrane recycling, defining a phosphoinositide-RAB switch controlling macropinocytosis.

papers.title: Individual gene translocations during metazoan evolution.
papers.summary: Analysis of over 6,000 gene families across 46 invertebrate species identifies 11,904 ancestral and subsequent individual gene translocations during metazoan evolution. Correlating translocation counts with phylogenetic branch lengths reveals a very low rate, below 1% of gene families per 100 million years, quantifying rare single-gene chromosomal movement.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.summary: A 3D CNN-CVAE combined with LSTM molecular generation designed rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Computational screening of fourteen derivatives prioritized one candidate with favorable docking, predicted safety, and ADMET properties, though explicitly requiring experimental validation given the modest docking-score differences.

papers.title: Intercellular GAS6-AXL signaling triggers podocyte cuproptosis in acute kidney injury upstream regulated by CEBPD.
papers.summary: In acute kidney injury, endothelial-derived GAS6 signals through podocyte AXL/TYRO3 receptors to trigger cuproptosis. The transcription factor CEBPD upregulated early in AKI transactivates AXL and enriches TGF-beta and JAK-STAT signaling, defining a CEBPD-GAS6-AXL axis driving podocyte cell death in the AKI-to-CKD transition.

papers.title: Gene transcriptional profiling of osmoregulatory stress response in salmonids: Development and assessment of high-throughput multispecies assays.
papers.summary: A 28-assay TaqMan OpenArray osmoregulatory stress transcriptional profiling chip was developed for salmonid aquaculture, covering osmoregulation, stress, immune, and growth genes across eight salmonid species. A 24-hour saltwater challenge in chinook salmon confirmed detection of acute osmotic stress signatures, providing a multispecies tool for husbandry and stress research.

papers.title: Transcriptomic analysis of zebrafish (Danio rerio) liver exposed to sediments from the Loa River.
papers.summary: Zebrafish exposed to arsenic-contaminated Loa River sediments show a transcriptomic adverse outcome pathway: initial metal homeostasis gene perturbation, followed by oxidative and ER stress, hypoxia-like signatures, angiogenesis gene activation, and finally epigenetic dysregulation and genomic instability markers, providing molecular fingerprints of sublethal aquatic contamination effects.

papers.title: Characterisation of multidrug-resistant, avian pathogenic-like Escherichia coli O78 from dairy-bred calves with atypical colisepticaemia.
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of multidrug-resistant E. coli O78:H9 ST23 from Scottish dairy calves with atypical septicaemia reveals a highly related avian pathogenic-like strain cluster with 13 virulence genes and a novel fimH variant. Despite no nearby poultry units, phylogeny suggests possible emergence of avian-like pathogenic E. coli in cattle meriting surveillance.

papers.title: Integrated morpho-biochemical, molecular, phylogenetic, and thermodynamic characterization of Bacillus isolates from ecologically distinct Indian soils.
papers.summary: Eight Bacillus isolates from ecologically distinct Indian soils underwent integrated morpho-biochemical, antimicrobial, phylogenetic, and RNA thermodynamic characterization. 16S rRNA sequencing identified B. safensis and B. subtilis/velezensis complex members with metabolic heterogeneity, stable ribosomal conformations, and antibiotic susceptibility patterns, providing a resource for agricultural and biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Mechanistic assessment of hepato-reproductive toxicity of Mentha pulegium L. essential oil in rats.
papers.summary: Mentha pulegium essential oil (pennyroyal), with pulegone as major constituent (42.72%), showed dose-dependent hepato-reproductive toxicity in rats via OECD 421 testing. Network pharmacology identified CYP19A1, ESR2, and HSD11B1 as key targets; in vivo exposure impaired fertility, increased oxidative stress, and disrupted steroid hormone biosynthesis, informing regulatory risk assessment.

papers.title: The sphingolipid code of cancer: divergent roles across tumor types and therapeutic horizons.
papers.summary: A comprehensive review examines how the ceramide-sphingosine-1-phosphate balance functions as a cancer-type-specific metabolic switch governing cell fate, proliferation, metastasis, and immune evasion across major malignancies. Therapeutic horizons include sphingosine kinase inhibitors, ceramide delivery systems, and ganglioside-directed immunotherapy, with challenges remaining in tumor heterogeneity and drug delivery.

papers.title: Limited effect of PCR ramp rate on qPCR Ct values: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: A systematic evaluation of PCR ramp rate effects on qPCR cycle threshold values across genotyping and gene expression assays found no consistent effect. Isolated statistically significant differences for specific assays were not reproduced across runs or comparisons, suggesting ramp rate has limited practical impact on Ct values under tested conditions.

papers.title: Integrated Proteomic and Phosphoproteomic Profiling Reveals Dysregulated Inflammatory Signaling Networks in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.summary: Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of rheumatoid arthritis patient PBMCs reveals dysregulated inflammatory signaling networks. Phosphorylation stoichiometry inversely correlates with protein abundance; ACTB and HSP90AA1 emerge as phosphoprotein hubs, while HDAC1, CBFB, PML, and STAT1 bridge phospho-signaling to inflammatory transcription, identifying druggable therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: mRNA-based therapies: From molecular discovery to clinical revolution.
papers.summary: A review traces mRNA therapeutics from molecular discovery through clinical revolution: modified nucleosides like pseudouridine improved stability and tolerability, COVID-19 vaccines demonstrated global clinical success, and mRNA platforms now expand toward protein replacement therapies and cancer treatment. Delivery vehicles, synthetic design, and administration strategies are summarized alongside remaining challenges.

papers.title: Micronucleus cytome assay reveals genomic instability in premalignant cervical lesions among high-risk HPV-positive women.
papers.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 184 Colombian women undergoing cervical cancer screening shows micronucleus cytome biomarkers, including micronuclei, nuclear buds, and binucleated cells, increase significantly across ordered HPV/cytology categories. Among HPV-positive women, genotype differences were observed in selected genotoxic and cytotoxic endpoints, supporting MNCyt as a complementary genomic instability risk assessment tool.
